newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Two killed, 49 hurt in attempt on Tajik president.
newsitem.headline: Two killed, 49 hurt in attempt on Tajik president.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov survived an assassination attempt on Wednesday which killed two people and injured 49 others.
Rakhmonov was wounded in the legs by a grenade but was able to stand up to condemn the attack in a theatre shortly afterwards, his spokesman said.
Zafar Saidov, his press secretary, said the dead were two men, a 17-year-old student and a 30-year-old teacher.
"At 10.30 am (0530 GMT), in the town of Khudjand in the Leninabad region, a terrorist act was carried out against President Imomali Rakhmonov," Saidov said.

Rakhmonov, 45, was on his way from a function marking the 65th anniversary of the northern town's university to the nearby Kamola Khudzhandi theatre when a grenade was thrown at his feet as he got out of a car.
A diplomatic source in Dushanbe said eyewitnesses contacted in the town spoke of many injured in the attack.
"The president, after being treated for his wounds, said the attack was the hand of a terrorist group and a provocative act," Saidov said.
The president had returned to speak at the theatre after the attack, he added.

Saidov said 21-year-old Firdavs Dustboboyev, who he said had organised an anti-government protest in the town in May last year, was responsible for the attack and was arrested almost immediately afterwards.

Tajikistan, a former Soviet republic, is still reeling from a four-year civil war in which tens of thousands of people were killed. Armed groups still roam the mountain state which borders Afghanistan and China.
A spokesman for Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, Rakhmonov's main foe in the civil war, told Reuters the group had no connection with the attack.

"We categorically deny any connection with the attack by the United Tajik Opposition," said Abdunabi Sattorzoda, a member of an opposition delegation in Dushanbe which has been involved in now stalled peace talks with the government.

Sattorzoda and diplomatic sources in the capital Dushanbe said the attack could be linked to unrest over a prison riot in Khudzhand earlier this month, led by prisoners involved in last year's anti-government demonstration.
Tajik security forces killed around 20 prisoners when they stormed the jail.

The violence is unusual for the northern Leninabad region, separated from the rest of the country by a chain of spectacular mountains. It has been spared much of the bloody conflict which has raged elsewhere.
